start.title: Put {{server}} in maintenance?
start.message: The partner takes over all clients while {{server}} is in maintenance. Use it before upgrading or restarting {{server}}.

cancel.title: End maintenance on {{server}}?
cancel.message: {{server}} goes back to its normal HA role and resynchronizes its leases with the partner.

false.title: Disable DHCP on {{server}}?
false.message: {{server}} stops answering DHCP clients (dhcp-disable). Clients rely on the partner until it is enabled again.

true.title: Remove HA from every server?
true.message: The ha hook is removed from {{server}}. Each server then serves its clients alone; leases are no longer copied.

true.title: Repair HA on {{server}}?
true.message: Pelagos checks that the node clocks agree, then restarts the HA service of each server in turn (config-reload) and waits until both serve in hot-standby or load-balancing. DHCP keeps being answered during the repair.

ha.leaseFeed: lease updates sent to the backup
ha.backupNote: Backup server: it receives every lease update from the active servers and answers no client. Promote it by giving it the role of a lost server.

setup.title: Set up HA
setup.intro: A relationship is a pair of active servers (primary and standby, or primary and secondary) with any number of backups, or a primary with backups in passive-backup. The plan writes the ha hook on every node that runs a server, each under its own name; servers no Pelagos node runs are written by hand with the same list. Kea 2.6 and 3.x take the same configuration for one relationship.
setup.backupHint: Extra servers join as backups: they take the lease updates and can be promoted.

modeHint.hot-standby: The primary serves every client; the standby takes over when the primary fails.
modeHint.load-balancing: The primary and the secondary share the clients; either serves all of them when the other fails.
modeHint.passive-backup: The primary serves every client and sends its lease updates to the backups; no automatic failover.

setup.hubHint: Kea 3 hub and spoke: a node runs a server in several relationships, under its own name and URL in each. Kea 2.6 takes one relationship per server.

terminated.title: HA terminated on {{servers}}
terminated.explain: The servers keep answering DHCP clients but exchange neither heartbeats nor lease updates: their lease databases drift apart until the HA service is restarted.
terminated.keaSkew: Kea measured a clock skew of {{seconds}} s with {{partner}} before terminating.
terminated.steps: Fix the clocks first (NTP, see the Clock column of the Nodes page), then repair: Pelagos restarts each server's HA service one after the other.

outage.d2Only: D2 reports failed updates; no active primary is known to be down yet.
outage.promoteHint: Promote a copy to take the updates again, then replay the leases of the outage.

stale.title: An old primary still serves zones handed over
stale.zone: {{zone}}: {{nodes}} serves it as primary, the role belongs to {{primary}} (epoch {{epoch}}).
stale.auto: Pelagos demotes it into a copy automatically.
stale.conflict: Same epoch on both sides: Pelagos does not decide alone, check both nodes.

replay.title: Replay of lost updates
replay.help: Counted: active leases whose last exchange with the client (cltt) falls inside the outage window and whose A, AAAA or PTR is missing or differs in the served zones. The plan resends them with lease4/6-resend-ddns.
replay.dialogHelp: {{count}} leases of the default window lack their records. Change the window if needed; the plan lists every lease before anything is sent.
replay.manualHelp: No outage gives a default window: enter the start (an empty end means now), within ddns.replay_window_max_hours. The plan lists every lease before anything is sent.
replay.badFrom: The start is not a valid date
replay.fromRequired: Enter the start of the window
replay.badTo: The end is not a valid date
replay.order: The start must be before the end
replay.tooLong: The window is longer than ddns.replay_window_max_hours allows (72 hours by default)
replay.badLimit: The maximum must be a positive whole number
replay.noOutage: D2 reported no outage: no update is known lost, so nothing is counted and there is no default window. A lease missing its record outside an outage raises the 'lease without record' alert. To resend the updates of a period anyway, choose a manual window.

d2.title: D2 server lists
d2.help: D2 tries the servers in order: the active primary must come first, a copy that answers REFUSED ends the request.

role.failoverHelp: The copy is rewritten as a primary zone with the recorded update policy, the D2 lists put it first and the epoch moves on. The old primary is demoted when it comes back.
role.switchoverHelp: Both nodes are online: the zone is frozen on the active primary for a few seconds, the target waits for the same serial, takes the role, and the old primary becomes its copy.
role.auto: Automatic: the copy with the highest serial
role.noTarget: No online node holds a copy of every selected zone.
role.failoverRisk: If the nodes only lost sight of each other, both may end up primary: promote only when the old primary is really down.
